reason: Sepals can be rugose (wrinkled). The examples are consistent.
Spathe is the bearer (FLOPO_0986007). The apex and the throat margin of a spathe can be truncate, so the examples fit.
Plant organ apex (FLOPO_0985023) is regularly acuminate. This is the standard apex shape.
The bearer is pollinium (FLOPO_0986016). Orchid pollinia are described by shape, such as clavate, spatulate and oblanceolate.
A leaf lamina can be uniformly coloured (unicolored). The examples fit.
Wrong reading. 'Spurred' means the base carries a spur. It does not mean the leaf is spur-shaped. Use a has-spur or has-part statement instead.
The bearer is indusium (FLOPO_0986020). A pale or pallid indusium is a low-saturation colour. The examples fit.

The bearer is pinnule (FLOPO_0985028). A pinnule can itself be pinnate, for example in a fern with three levels of division. Some examples describe venation on the pinnule, which should have vein as the bearer.
The mouth or apex of a grass leaf sheath can be oblique. The PATO term is imperfect, because it really describes a slanting cut, but the reading is consistent.
A lemma is commonly striate. The examples fit.
PATO_0000001 is the root term 'quality' and says nothing. The examples are alternatives (erect or reflexed, slender or stout) and belong to specific terms such as orientation or thickness.
The bearer is anther cap (FLOPO_0986034). A toothed or dentate anther cap is a genuine orchid trait.
The bearer is column foot (FLOPO_0986081). An orchid column foot can be curved or upcurved.
The bearer is gynostemium or column (FLOPO_0986015). The examples are heights ('2-2.5 mm tall'), so this is a valid measurement.
A leaf lamina lobe can be auriculate. The examples fit.
A whole plant or its habit can be pyramidal. The examples fit.
Rhizoids (in mosses) can be glossy. The examples fit.
There is only one flora, and 'dense' for a node could mean crowded nodes, dense hairs or dense tissue. A rule would need to tell nodes close together (internode length) from density of covering.
A spikelet has a colour. PATO colour is an attribute, and values such as straw-coloured are subtypes.
A nut can be oblate (flattened sphere). The examples fit.
A seed coat can be fleshy, as in a sarcotesta. The examples fit.
The shape of a caryopsis is standard. The examples fit.
The bearer is style branch (FLOPO_0986008). A style branch can be fringed with papillae or hairs.
The bearer is corolla lip (FLOPO_0985017). A lip, galea or lobe can be straight. The examples fit.
The length of an apex is a valid measurement. Some examples are ratios to the beak, which is fine, but the bare '1.0–1.5' row has no part and should be reviewed.
A rhizome can be narrow. The examples fit.
The bearer is corolla plica (FLOPO_0986067). Plicae can be oblique. The examples fit.
The bearer is stylopodium (FLOPO_0986022). Its diameter is a normal measurement in Apiaceae.
The bearer is indusium (FLOPO_0986020). Its diameter is a normal measurement in ferns.
A tepal can taper. The examples fit.
The bearer is tree crown (FLOPO_0985030). A crown can be hemispherical. The examples fit.
The bearer is mentum (FLOPO_0986031). Its apex can be obtuse.
Wrong reading. 'Alar cells few' is a count of the cells, not fewer parts of one cell. Handle it as a count of alar cells on the leaf.
Wrong part. The examples ('spur ellipsoid', 'épaississement ellipsoïdal') describe a spur or a thickening, not a short shoot. The PO term was chosen by a word match.
A moss peristome tooth can be fragile or delicate. The examples fit.
A branch can have a mealy or farinose covering. The examples fit.
Wrong reading. The examples describe crenate ribs ('nervure crénelée') or a margin, not the ovary as a whole. The bearer should be the rib or the margin.
The bearer is leaf scar (FLOPO_0986052). Its width is a valid measurement. Check that the width rows with no part really refer to the scar.
The bearer is cyathium (FLOPO_0985029). A cyathium has a colour. Check that the 'outer surface is light green' rows refer to the cyathium.
Archegonia can be terminal on the stem. The examples fit.
A nectary can be small. The examples fit.
Wrong reading. 'Uncinate trichomes' describes hairs, not the ovary. Only the single 'ovary hooked toward apex' row is arguably the ovary.
A pappus can be sericeous or silky. The examples fit.
The bearer is corolla plica (FLOPO_0986067). A plica apex can be obtuse or rounded. There is only one flora.
The bearer is corolla lobe (FLOPO_0986006). PATO 'structure' is too generic. The examples (connate, free) are about fusion and should use a fused or free value term.
Wrong reading. 'Depressed' on the upper face means sunken or impressed veins, not curved. Use a sunken or impressed term.
Glands can be ellipsoid. The examples fit.
A follicle is described by three dimensions (length × width × depth or thickness). The examples are valid.
Paraphyses can be stellate. The examples fit.
A whole plant can be glaucous or pruinose. The examples fit.
A drupe can be smooth. The examples fit.
Wrong bearer. Bistratose or unistratose counts layers of cells in a lamina, so a single cell has no stratification. The bearer should be the leaf lamina or the tissue.
Wrong reading. 'Legume a loment' names the fruit type. 'Present' says nothing about a quality of the loment.
Decumbent is normally a stem or branch habit. It is rare for a leaflet, and there is only one flora. A rule would need to tell leaflet orientation from the stem.
A lamina can have an oblique base. This is a real botanical trait, although the PATO term is imperfect.
'Calyx irregular' usually means zygomorphic (symmetry), not an irregular spatial pattern. 'Teeth irregular' belongs on the teeth. A rule would need to tell symmetry from the arrangement of parts.
Young shoots can be scaly. The examples fit.
Wrong reading. 'Subentire' describes the margin, a nearly smooth edge, and has nothing to do with 'unstructured'. Use the margin as the bearer with an entire value.
Shoots can be conspicuous. The examples fit, although the lenticel example has the wrong bearer.
A receptacle can be ellipsoid. The examples fit.
